recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — web/ scaffold + shared foundations
recommended_phases.rationale: Stand up the separate Vite build (package.json, tsconfig, vite config, index.html, main.tsx) plus shared-types and shared-date. No dependencies on other modules; everything else imports these.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — infrastructure API client + token storage
recommended_phases.rationale: IApiClient/ApiClient (bearer header, 401 handling) and ITokenStorage/TokenStorage. Depends only on shared-types; unblocks all service modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — auth module
recommended_phases.rationale: IAuthService/AuthService (login/logout/token/profile) plus AuthProvider/useAuth. Depends on api-client and shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — employee + leave + balance services
recommended_phases.rationale: Read-only service modules (getMe, list, getById, getMyBalances) over the API client. Depends on api-client and shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — presentation: router, pages, guards
recommended_phases.rationale: LoginPage, DashboardPage, LeaveListPage, LeaveDetailPage, protected-route guard, UTC date rendering. Depends on all service modules and shared foundations.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 — component tests + README
recommended_phases.rationale: Vitest + Testing Library coverage for login success/failure, 401 redirect, and bearer-token sending; README run instructions. Depends on all prior phases.

app_notes: The frontend lives in a separate top-level web/ build (Vite + React + TypeScript), outside src/ so it is not subject to the backend modular-monolith dependency map. Layers flow inward: presentation -> module services -> infrastructure api-client -> shared-types/shared-date. No circular edges (verified: every edge points from an outer layer toward an inner layer; shared-types and shared-date are leaf dependencies). All public service methods are declared on interfaces before implementation. Cross-module value types (EmployeeProfile, LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LoginResponse, and the enums) live in web/src/shared/types/; types with owned behavior (services, api client, token storage) get their own module directories. The frontend is read-only: it consumes the existing POST /auth/login, GET /employees/me, GET /leaves, GET /leaves/:id, and GET /balances/me endpoints and never mutates backend state.

open_questions.question: Where should the JWT token be persisted in the browser (localStorage vs sessionStorage vs in-memory)?
open_questions.impact: Affects session lifetime, XSS exposure surface, and whether the user stays logged in across tabs/restarts. The 401-redirect and logout behavior depend on the chosen storage.

open_questions.question: How should the frontend render UTC date strings so the displayed day never shifts with the browser timezone?
open_questions.impact: A wrong choice reintroduces the prior UTC+3 off-by-one-day defect. The formatting rule must be applied consistently across the list and detail views.
candidate_options: Parse with Date.UTC and format via getUTC* accessors
Render the raw YYYY-MM-DD substring of the ISO string

auth_contract: The frontend consumes the backend's existing auth contract; it does not define a new one. Identity shape: request.user = { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. The backend's registerAuth preHandler verifies the JWT bearer token and populates request.user; RBAC is enforced server-side. The frontend's only auth responsibilities are: send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on every authenticated call, store the token returned by POST /auth/login, and redirect to the login screen on any 401 (clearing the token). No role-gated screens are built in this run.
error_response_contract: The frontend consumes the backend's existing error contract; it does not define a new one. Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure -> HTTP 400; authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError); authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError); not found -> 404 (NotFoundError); invalid state transition -> 409 (ConflictError); other -> 500. The frontend must surface the server's error message on login failure without distinguishing wrong-email from wrong-password (the API returns identical 401 bodies), and must treat any 401 on an authenticated call as a signal to clear the token and return to login.
